subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the princess whose face, hairstyle, hair ornaments, and costume come from <Picture 1>: an oval face with willow-leaf brows, slightly downcast eye corners, red-tinted lips, and cool pale skin; dark hair coiled into a high bun, with long pearl tassel pins hanging on both sides, gold floral hairpins, and pale-jade earrings; an ivory wide-sleeved robe trimmed in pale green, with interlocking cloud embroidery along the collar and cuffs, a pale-green waist sash, and a round green-jade pendant hanging at her left side, over pale embroidered shoes. <Picture 1> is a four-panel studio reference sheet on a grey background and is used only to lock her identity, hair, and costume; its grey studio backdrop, panel layout, and multi-view arrangement must not appear in the target video, which contains one person in one continuous frame at all times.
<Subject 2> is the enclosed palace courtyard shown in <Picture 2>: high rammed-earth walls with dark grey upturned roof ridges on both sides, bamboo fences lining a flagstone and packed-earth path, two old cherry trees with low horizontal branches, continuous falling petals covering the ground, soft afternoon light raking through the branches, and distant mountains and drifting cloud visible above the wall line.

<Subject 1> is the ink-wash bamboo grove in <Picture 1>, with its material quality and brushwork: deep pine-green and teal ink laid on coarse-grained ivory rice paper, three or four stalks rising on the right side, layered clusters of long pointed leaves in near and far ink densities, a soft pale-gold moon disc half hidden behind the leaves, scattered hand-torn gold leaf flecks, and a wide area of diluted wash spreading across the lower left. The paper fibre, watermark edges, and dry-brush grain remain visible across every element; nothing is sharpened, traced, or re-rendered into clean digital vector or glossy 3D.

summary:
[reference generation] A 9:16 ink-wash moving image built from the bamboo grove in <Subject 1>: the front leaves sway and the movement travels down the stems, gold flecks lift off the lower wash and drift across the paper, and the moon and haze shift faintly, in a single held shot of eight seconds.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the pine-green ink palette, coarse rice-paper texture, dry-brush grain, layered leaf clusters, pale-gold moon behind the leaves, hand-torn gold flecks, and lower-left diluted wash are retained, while the exact leaf positions and stem spacing are allowed to differ as the plants move; no element gains sharpened edges, traced veins, clean vector lines, or glossy surface.

detailed_description:
An ink-wash painting on coarse rice paper in the hand-painted Chinese style of <Subject 1>. Paper fibre is legible in the ivory areas, ink edges stay soft and bloomed, and no element is ever sharpened or traced.
[Shot 1] A vertical composition with the bamboo mass filling the right two thirds and the diluted wash opening at the lower left; the pale moon sits behind the leaves at roughly one third from the top, diffuse and never crisp. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed, one breath of movement, so the composition remains recognizable. The front leaf cluster sways first, tilting a few degrees outward and rocking back; the motion travels down the stem and reaches the middle cluster a beat later, so no two clusters move at the same time. The two heaviest leaves keep a fine gold rim along their edges as the light shifts across them. Gold flecks lift off the lower-left wash one at a time and drift upward across the ivory paper at an uneven rate, each fleck keeping its irregular hand-torn shape and its dull metallic dullness rather than becoming a glowing particle. The haze above the moon thickens faintly and then thins, and the moon stays a diffuse disc behind the ink throughout. At the end the front cluster is still swinging back into place.

overall_soundscape: A thin high wind moves through bamboo, closer to paper rustle than branch creak, with long stretches of near silence between gusts. A very light dry crackle of paper grain continues underneath.

non_diegetic_music: A single low guqin note at long intervals over a barely audible sustained drone, at a slow tempo, never rising above the breeze.

detailed_description:
No hard cut. Immediately following the previous section. The framing never tightens past the chest line.
[Shot 1] A medium close shot from the front. Her hand is already lifted, fingertips turning slowly in the drifting petals, and they close on a single intact blossom. She is reaching for something for the only time in the whole piece.
[Shot 2] At 00:04.500, the camera cuts to a medium close shot framed lower, holding her hands, the pale-green sash, and the round jade pendant at her waist. The petal lies across her fingers; her thumb passes along its edge once, then again, and her fingers fold a little closer around it, as if she might keep it.
[Shot 3] At 00:08.000, the camera cuts to a medium close shot at a front three-quarter angle. Her eyes are not on the petal - they have gone past it, up to the wall above the trees, and stay there, steady and awake, while her mouth works against what her eyes are doing. <Subject 1> (S1) says in the same low, breathy voice, <d>[Chinese] 沉醉不知归路。</d> On the last word she takes one slow blink and the line of her jaw tightens once.
[Shot 4] At 00:12.000, the camera cuts to a medium close shot from a slightly side angle. Her eyes come back down to the petal in her hand and rest on it without softening; the folded fingers ease by a degree, then stop, and the hand stays closed.

overall_soundscape:
The same courtyard ambience persists at a lower level. Petals settling on silk produce faint dry ticks, her slow breathing is audible, and a single quiet swallow lands just after the line.

non_diegetic_music:
The guzheng continues in single notes while a low xiao tone enters beneath it, at a slightly reduced volume, holding under the end of her line without fading out.

detailed_description:
No hard cut. Immediately following the previous section. The camera rises from eye level to a tilt-up and settles back down, and the spatial relationship of the courtyard does not jump.
[Shot 1] A medium shot from behind her shoulder. She turns her head first and then her whole body, slowly, as though she does not much want to look. Her wide sleeves hang straight, the pearl tassel pins come to rest against her neck, and the camera pans right with small amplitude at slow speed to keep her centered as she completes the turn. Then <Subject 1> (S1) says in the same low, breathy voice, <d>[Chinese] 兴尽晚回舟。</d>
[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, the camera cuts to an empty shot with no one in frame, tilting up with large amplitude at slow speed. The rammed-earth wall fills the upper half of the frame, its surface showing packed horizontal strata, streaks worn by rain, and fine straw fibre; the bamboo fence casts long diagonal shadows along the bottom, and only a thin band of sky remains at the top edge. A few petals drift in from beyond the wall and fall into the courtyard, which reads as a space she cannot leave.
[Shot 3] At 00:06.500, the camera cuts to a shot crossing her shoulder and pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the mountains beyond the wall. The distant ridges and moving cloud stay sharp while she remains soft in the lower right foreground, her back and the edge of her profile turned away. Her lips move and <Subject 1> (S1) says in the same low, breathy voice, carrying clearly over the wind, <d>[Chinese] 误入藕花深处。</d>
[Shot 4] At 00:09.500, the camera cuts to a medium close shot of her at a front three-quarter angle as she brings her gaze back from the far ridges. She blinks once, lowers her eyes, and her fingers close slowly inside her sleeve. The shot holds with her posture still and unresolved, ready to hand off to the next segment.

overall_soundscape:
The wind strengthens against the high wall and thickens in tone, carrying a distant thread of birdsong and the faint low wash of streets beyond the palace. Silk flaps continuously, and the sound thins for a moment on the words spoken against it.

non_diegetic_music:
Low strings rise slowly while the guzheng shifts into a slow broken-chord pattern, at a steady tempo and increasing volume, never fading out.
